findings.summary: K1, confirmed and wider than reported: QuoteScanner::classOf() classes a curly mark by its shape, not by its role in the active locale and variant, so a straight quote right beside a German or Czech mark is decided from the wrong class. Where an opening mark is classed CLOSE (de `book` » ›), a straight `"` right after it closes the quotation instead of opening a nested one. Where a closing mark is classed OPEN (de, de-CH and cs CLDR “ ‘, and de `book` « ‹), a straight closing `"` or `'` right after it and before punctuation opens a new quotation. Because Context::before() hands classBefore() the already converted text of the previous run, straight-only input across an inline tag is hit too, with no curly mark typed. The page pass and fix-on-save both write it, and a second pass cannot repair it, since no straight mark is left.
findings.location: src/engine/rules/QuoteScanner.php:410-441 (classOf: “ ‘ „ ‚ « ‹ → OPEN, ” ’ » › → CLOSE, whatever the locale), :359-383 (classBefore), :262-265 and :306 (decideDouble/decideSingle branch on OPEN vs CLOSE); src/engine/Context.php:85-92 (before() returns flow->done, the converted text of earlier runs); tests/engine/corpus/14-same-type-nesting.txt (every curly-parent case puts the straight child after a space, never next to the mark)
findings.cause: classOf() hard-codes the English/French shapes of quotation marks. In German (default „…“ ‚…‘, and Czech and de-CH the same) the closing marks “ ‘ have the shape of English openers. In the German book style »…« ›…‹ both pairs point the opposite way to French. A straight quote decided next to one of these is given the opposite context, and across a tag boundary the mark in the context is the scan’s own output.

findings.summary:
K2, confirmed: in fi and sv the marks ” and ’ both open and close, so the scanner counts neither as a parent, and a straight quotation inside a curly one gets the primary marks again (`”Han sa: "nej."”` → `”Han sa: ”nej.””`; ’…’ is expected inside). The same happens with straight input only, across an inline tag, because the converted ” before the tag is classed CLOSE (`

""Ja," sagte er."

` → `””Ja,” sagte er.”`). The README promises with no exception that a quotation set in curly marks counts as its level. Only DEVELOPMENT.md states the exception. The behaviour is the same at 98db482; D822 added the promise it breaks.
findings.location: src/engine/rules/QuoteScanner.php:111-131 (`$opens && !$closes` / `$closes && !$opens`: a glyph in both roles is skipped); README.md:79 (“A quotation already set in curly marks counts as the level its marks have in the language”); docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:195 (the exception, dev docs only)
findings.cause: A glyph that is both the opening and the closing mark cannot be told apart by identity, and the scanner does not try context. Across a tag, classOf(”) is CLOSE even when the scan itself just wrote it as an opener.

That comes with fi and sv corpus cases for T0–T6, T14, T15 and the inline-tag T0 (for example `”Er sagte: "Nein."”` → `”Er sagte: ’Nein.’”`). findings.summary: The quote scan is quadratic in nesting depth, and D822’s parallel `$levels` array doubled the cost. In one text node, pop() rebuilds the stack, and now the levels as well, with array_splice() on every close. Across inline tags, both arrays are copied once per run. An adversarial paragraph of unclosed nested quotation marks (a comment or form submission the template prints, under the 1,000,000-byte maxPageBytes) takes 20.5 s at 480 KB (10.4 s at 98db482). So at about 580 KB (about 820 KB before) the page pass runs past a 30 s max_execution_time. That fatal cannot be caught, which breaks “It never breaks a page”. tests/engine/unit.php says “The quote scan is linear on a long text node”, but no guard covers nesting.
findings.location: src/engine/rules/QuoteScanner.php:224-237 (pop(): array_splice($levels, $i) and array_splice($stack, $i), each O(array size)); :87-93 and :213 (flow state stack and levels copied on write per run); tests/engine/unit.php:439-442 (the only quote-scan speed guard, a possessive paragraph); README.md:104
findings.cause: array_splice() reindexes the whole array even when it removes only the last element, so each close costs O(depth); D822 added a second array to splice and to copy per run.
